title: Xianbei
capsule: The Xianbei were a proto-Mongolic nomadic confederation originating in the Donghu tribal complex of eastern Inner Asia; they rose to prominence after the Han dynasty's destruction of the Xiongnu confederation in the late 1st century CE, filling the resulting power vacuum across the eastern steppe. Under Tanshihuai (r. c. 156–181 CE) the Xianbei united into a loose empire stretching from Manchuria to the Altai, repeatedly raiding Han frontier territories and defeating Han punitive expeditions. After Tanshihuai's death the confederation fragmented, but Xianbei lineages went on to found a series of conquest dynasties within China including the Murong, Tuoba, and Khitan states; the Tuoba branch established the Northern Wei dynasty (386 CE), which reunified northern China. The dataset's attestation runs from 60 to 237 CE, capturing the confederation's formation, apogee, and initial fragmentation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent of the Xianbei confederation is conjectural and based on Chinese dynastic annals (Hou Hanshu, Sanguozhi) that describe raiding zones rather than administered boundaries; steppe extents are approximate and subject to scholarly debate.
